explainer.diffIntro: Lower fees and 24/7 trading are true of every peer-to-peer desk. These are the things a centralised exchange cannot say.
explainer.benefit1Body: The money goes straight from your account to your counterparty's. There is no platform balance to freeze, and no company between you that could fail while holding it.
explainer.benefit2Title: Escrow is a program, not a promise
explainer.benefit2Body: The crypto sits in a Solana escrow program that releases on the outcome. Not on an operator's decision, and not on ours — we could not release it early if we wanted to.
explainer.benefit3Body: Every advertiser has bonded OPEN that a lost dispute can slash, and eight reputation dimensions that move on every trade. That is what stands behind a stranger, in place of a company's guarantee.
explainer.benefit4Title: Disputes are decided by staked strangers
explainer.benefit4Body: Independent arbitrators stake OPEN to join a case, review evidence they cannot see until they commit, and vote by commit-and-reveal. No support queue, and no operator with a final say.
explainer.benefit5Body: Mobile money, instant bank transfer and the payment apps people actually use, in every country — plus cash, which works where nothing electronic does.
explainer.benefit6Body: The order book lives on a peer-to-peer network, not on a server we own. There is no operator to lean on and no jurisdiction that switches it off.

index.whatIsBody: P2P trading lets you buy and sell crypto directly with other people using your local currency and payment methods. Instead of trusting a stranger, every order is protected by escrow: the seller's crypto locks in the Solana escrow program the moment the order is placed, and it is released only after the seller confirms your payment arrived. OpenFiat never takes custody of your fiat.
glossary: A verified user who posts buy/sell offers with their own price, limits, and payment methods.
You — the user who picks an existing offer and places an order against it.
The seller's crypto locks in the Solana escrow program when the order is placed and releases only after payment is confirmed.
The button to press when something goes wrong — escrow freezes and an arbitrator steps in.

safetyTips: Never release crypto before confirming payment in your own account.
Only pay the exact account details shown in the order — never details sent in chat.
Avoid third-party payments: the sender's name should match the counterparty.
Use Appeal if the counterparty doesn't respond or something feels wrong.
Keep all chat on-platform — it becomes evidence in a dispute.

buy.metaTitle: How to Buy Crypto with Fiat — Fiat On-Ramp | OpenFiat
buy.metaDescription: Fiat on-ramp made simple: buy stablecoins peer-to-peer with local payment methods on the OpenFiat P2P exchange — escrow-protected on Solana.
buy.heroTitle: How to Buy Crypto with Fiat — Fiat On-Ramp
buy.heroDescription: Turn your local currency into stablecoins in minutes. Which tokens, currencies and payment methods are on offer comes from your access node and the live order book — every order protected by escrow on Solana.
steps: Choose Buy + asset + your currency + payment method

The asset pills, the currency list and the payment-method filter are all read from your access node and from the live book — so they show what is genuinely on offer where you are, rather than a list written into this page.
Compare offers
Compare price, available liquidity and per-order limits — the three things every row on the book actually carries.
Click Buy and enter an amount
Enter how much fiat you want to spend (or how much crypto you want) — within the advertiser's limits.
Place the order
The seller's crypto locks in the Solana escrow program immediately, so it is guaranteed for you before you pay anything.
Pay the seller within the time window
Transfer fiat using exactly the account details shown in the order — every field is copyable. If the window expires, the order cancels and escrow unlocks.
Click “Transferred, notify seller”
Only after you have actually sent the money. This tells the seller to check their account.
Seller confirms — crypto arrives in your wallet
The seller verifies your payment and escrow releases the crypto to your wallet. Order completed.
goodToKnow: Escrow protects you: the seller's crypto is locked on Solana before you pay — they cannot disappear with it.
What you pay is the advertiser's price. Protocol fees live on chain in the escrow program's fee config and are governance-updatable, so no page here quotes a rate it has not read.
Every order has a payment window; if you can't pay in time, cancel instead of letting it expire.
If the seller doesn't respond or confirm, open an Appeal — escrow freezes and an arbitrator steps in.

sell.heroTitle: How to Sell Crypto for Fiat — Fiat Off-Ramp
sell.heroDescription: Cash out your stablecoins to local currency safely. Which tokens and payment methods are on offer comes from your access node and the live order book — escrow-protected on Solana.
steps: Choose Sell
Pick the token you want to sell and the fiat currency you want to receive. Both lists come from your access node, not from this page.
Pick an offer matching your amount
Compare buyer prices, available liquidity and per-order limits the same way buyers compare sellers.
Enter the amount and place the order
Your crypto locks in the Solana escrow program — the buyer can see it is guaranteed for them.
Wait for the buyer's payment
The buyer transfers fiat to your bank or mobile-money account within the time window.
Verify the funds in YOUR account
Log in to your own bank or mobile-money account and confirm the money actually arrived — never trust screenshots alone.
Click “Payment received” and release
Only after verifying. Escrow releases your crypto to the buyer instantly.
Order completed
Fiat is in your account, the buyer has their crypto, and both reputations update.
goodToKnow: Never release crypto before confirming payment in your own account — this is the one rule that matters.
Screenshots prove nothing: buyers can fake payment proofs. Check your own balance.
Beware of third-party payments: the sender's name should match the buyer.
If the buyer marks paid but nothing arrived, don't release — open an Appeal and an arbitrator will review.
Keep all chat on-platform so it can serve as evidence in a dispute.

merchant.metaTitle: How to Become a Merchant — Post Ads on OpenFiat P2P | OpenFiat
merchant.metaDescription: Become an OpenFiat merchant: bond OPEN, fund a liquidity vault, and publish advertisements buyers and sellers can trade against. No application and no approval — the bond is the qualification.
merchant.heroDescription: Merchants are the liquidity on OpenFiat: they post the advertisements everyone else trades against, quote the prices, and settle the fiat leg. There is no application and no approval — you bond OPEN, fund a vault, and publish. What follows is what that actually commits you to.
merchant.bondNote: Bonding is a real staking transaction, and this page does not read your wallet — so it cannot tell you whether you already qualify. <link>The staking page</link> shows the minimum bond the deployed program actually enforces and what you have bonded against it.
steps: Bond OPEN

A merchant stakes OPEN as accountability, not as a fee — it stays yours unless a protocol penalty applies. The staking page shows the minimum the deployed program enforces; this page deliberately does not restate a figure it has not read. This is what replaces an application form: nobody approves you, but you have something at risk.
Fund a liquidity vault

A sell advertisement is backed by inventory you have already deposited, per stablecoin. Reservations move balances from Available to Reserved, and settlement moves them to Settled — a buyer can see the funds exist before committing, which is why your ads get taken.
Decide your market
Direction, asset and fiat currency. Pick a corridor you can actually service: you need a payment account in that currency, and you need to be awake when its buyers are.
Set a price

Fixed, or floating as a premium over the oracle mid. Floating tracks the market without you watching it; fixed is predictable but goes stale. Tighter pricing wins more orders and earns less per order.
Set limits you will honour
Minimum and maximum per trade. A maximum above what you can settle promptly costs you settlement speed, which is a reputation dimension buyers filter on.
Declare payment methods and terms

Only rails you can genuinely receive on. Your terms are where you state whose name must be on the transfer, what reference to use, and which hours you settle — those conditions are what disputes turn on, so put them here rather than explaining them in chat afterwards.
Publish and stay responsive
Availability and response time are scored and decay with inactivity, so a stale ad quietly stops appearing. Pause your ads rather than leaving them up when you cannot settle.
obligations: Your bond is slashable. Failing to settle a trade you accepted, or losing a dispute, has a cost — that is the point of it.
Every completed trade updates eight reputation dimensions. Dispute rate and settlement speed are the two buyers look at hardest.
You are the counterparty, not a platform. Nobody escrows on your behalf — the Solana escrow program does, and it releases on the outcome, not on your say-so.
Release only after you have verified the money in your own account. A screenshot is not a payment.
Keep every message in the trade chat. It is the evidence an arbitrator reads, and conversations moved elsewhere cannot be produced later.

tradeActions.heading: What you can do
tradeActions.cannotSign: This wallet connection cannot sign — reconnect it and try again.
tradeActions.notNumericIdNote: This reservation's id is not a number, so it addresses no escrow account on chain — the escrow program finds a trade escrow at a PDA seeded with the id as a u64. Nothing on chain can be created, read or released for it. Reservations placed by this app always can be.
tradeActions.escrowReading: Reading the escrow from the cluster… If this does not resolve, the cluster could not be reached — which is not the same as there being no escrow.
tradeActions.escrowNone: No escrow exists on chain for this reservation yet.
tradeActions.onChainTitle: Moves value on Solana, and costs a network fee

initiate.label: Open the settlement
initiate.detail: Records the buyer and the merchant against this reservation and starts the payment window. Signed by you, sent to the node — nothing moves on chain.

lock-escrow.label: Lock the escrow
lock-escrow.detail: Reserves the amount in your liquidity vault, opens the trade escrow, and moves the tokens into it. One transaction, so a reservation can never be left marked against inventory with no escrow behind it.

declare-paid.label: I have sent the payment
declare-paid.detail: Tells the merchant the fiat is on its way. Only do this once you have actually sent it — the declaration is signed by you and permanent.

approve.label: Confirm the payment arrived
approve.detail: Two signatures: the node records your approval, and the escrow program marks the trade approved so the tokens can be released.

release.label: Release the escrow
release.detail: Pays the buyer and the four fee treasuries out of the escrow. Anyone may submit it once the merchant has approved, and it goes through the node so the network records the confirmation.

cancel-escrow.label: Return the tokens to the vault
cancel-escrow.detail: Cancels the on-chain escrow and puts the merchant's tokens back in their liquidity vault. Only possible before release.

cancel-reservation.label: Cancel this reservation
cancel-reservation.detail: Withdraws your claim on the merchant's liquidity and frees it immediately, instead of holding it for the rest of the 30-minute window. Signed by you, sent to the node — nothing moves on chain, and only you can cancel your own reservation.

cancel-settlement.label: Cancel the trade
cancel-settlement.detail: Ends the settlement with nothing owed either way. Possible only while no payment has been declared — once the buyer has said they paid, neither side can walk away unilaterally.

reverse-payment.label: I have not actually paid
reverse-payment.detail: Withdraws your declaration and returns the trade to awaiting payment. Only do this for a declaration made in error: it lets the merchant cancel the trade, so a payment that really has left your account must go to a dispute instead.

reject-payment.label: The payment never arrived
reject-payment.detail: Records your refusal without opening a dispute or paying a filing fee. It is your claim, not a ruling — a buyer who really did pay can still open a dispute afterwards.

dispute.label: Open a dispute
dispute.detail: Puts the trade in front of arbitrators. Both parties' evidence comes from the trade channel, and disclosing it to an arbitrator shares the whole conversation permanently.

waiting.observer: You are not a party to this trade, so there is nothing here for you to sign.
waiting.merchantNoSettlement: The taker has reserved against your advertisement but has not opened the settlement yet. Until they do, there is no record naming you as the seller to act on — and only they can cancel their own reservation.
waiting.merchantEscrowUnknown: The cluster could not be read, so whether this trade's escrow already exists is unknown. Locking it again would fail on an account that is already there — reload before signing anything.
waiting.merchantEscrowHeld: The escrow holds your tokens. The buyer has not declared the fiat sent yet — which is also the only window in which either of you can still walk away.
waiting.buyerEscrowUnreadable: Whether the merchant has locked the tokens could not be read from the cluster. Do not send any money until it can be.
waiting.buyerNotLocked: The merchant has not locked the tokens in escrow yet. Do not send any money until they have — there is nothing on chain backing this trade.
waiting.buyerAwaitingConfirm: The merchant has been told the payment is sent and has not confirmed it yet.
waiting.approvedNoEscrow: This settlement is approved but no escrow was ever funded for it, so there is nothing to release.
waiting.disputed: This trade is with arbitrators. The escrow moves on their decision, not on either party's signature.

discrepancy.WrongReference: The reference was wrong or missing
discrepancy.DuplicatePayment: It was a duplicate of another payment
discrepancy.IncorrectAccount: It was sent to the wrong account

tradeActions.referencePlaceholder: What your bank or wallet put on the transfer
tradeActions.referenceHelp: Whatever you type here is stored on the settlement and readable by the merchant and by any arbitrator — it is dropped from the public view for that reason, so keep it to the reference itself.
tradeActions.rejectDiscrepancyHelp: This is the field reputation counts, so pick the one that actually applies. Everything except “Something else” records a payment-accuracy fault against the buyer.
tradeActions.rejectOwnWordsHelp: Read by the buyer and by any arbitrator they escalate to. Nothing parses it.
tradeActions.reverseWarning: Only if you have not actually sent the money. Withdrawing your declaration returns the trade to awaiting payment, which lets the merchant cancel it — so if the fiat really has left your account, this hands them a window to cancel out from under it. In that case open a dispute instead.
tradeActions.cancelSettlementWarning: Ends the trade with nothing owed either way. If the other side has already sent the fiat but has not declared it yet, this cancels out from under their money — the protocol cannot see a bank transfer, only the declaration. Do not cancel a trade somebody has told you they are paying.
tradeActions.cancelReservationNote: Frees the merchant's liquidity straight away instead of holding it for the rest of the 30-minute window. There is nothing to undo afterwards — you would place a new order.
tradeActions.busyPrompt: {what}… approve the prompt in your wallet.
tradeActions.errNotNumericId: This reservation's id is not a number, so it addresses no escrow account. Reservations placed by this app are; one from another client may not be.
tradeActions.errNoAdMint: This trade's advertisement could not be read, and it is the only record of which mint the escrow settles in. Nothing on chain can be built without it.
tradeActions.errNoAdMerchantKey: This trade's advertisement could not be read, and the settlement has to name the merchant's own public key from it.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementLock: There is no settlement to lock an escrow against.
tradeActions.errBuyerNoAddress: The buyer's peer id carries no Solana address, so no escrow can name them.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementDeclare: There is no settlement to declare a payment on.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementApprove: There is no settlement to approve.
tradeActions.errWalletBroadcasts: This wallet cannot sign a transaction without also broadcasting it. The release has to reach Solana through the node so the network records the confirmation, so it cannot be completed from this wallet.
tradeActions.errPartyNoAddressRelease: A party's peer id carries no Solana address, so no release can be built.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementRelease: There is no settlement to release.
tradeActions.errNoEscrowCancel: There is no escrow to cancel.
tradeActions.errPartyNoAddressCancel: A party's peer id carries no Solana address, so no cancellation can be built.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementCancel: There is no settlement to cancel.
tradeActions.errNoDeclaration: There is no declaration to withdraw.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementReject: There is no settlement to reject.
tradeActions.errRejectEmpty: Say what you did or did not find — the buyer and any arbitrator read this.
tradeActions.errNoSettlementDispute: There is no settlement to dispute.
tradeActions.errDisputeEmpty: Say what went wrong — an arbitrator reads this.
tradeActions.okInitiate: The settlement is open. The merchant can now lock the tokens in escrow.
tradeActions.okDeclare: The merchant has been told the payment is on its way.
tradeActions.okApprove: Approved, on the node and on chain. Transaction {signature}. Either party can now release the escrow.
tradeActions.okApproveNodeOnly: Approved on the node. The on-chain approval could not be built: the buyer's peer id carries no Solana address.
tradeActions.okRelease: The release is with the node. It will be recorded on this trade once the node has seen it confirmed for itself.
tradeActions.okReleaseUnwrap: The release is with the node. It will be recorded on this trade once the node has seen it confirmed for itself — the wrapped SOL is unwrapped in the same transaction, so what arrives is SOL.
tradeActions.okCancelEscrow: The tokens are back in the merchant's vault. Transaction {signature}. The off-chain records are separate — cancel the trade as well, or the settlement stays open with no escrow behind it.
tradeActions.okCancelReservation: The reservation is cancelled and the merchant's liquidity is free again.
tradeActions.okCancelSettlement: The trade is cancelled. If tokens are still locked in escrow, return them to the vault as well — the two records are separate.
tradeActions.okReverse: Your declaration is withdrawn and the trade is awaiting payment again. The merchant can now cancel it, so send the money and declare again, or cancel yourself.
tradeActions.okReject: Recorded. The buyer can still open a dispute if they believe they paid — rejecting moves the cost of escalating onto whoever is wrong, it does not decide who that is.
tradeActions.okDispute: Dispute {id} is open. Arbitrators join it from the arbitration desk.

tradeChannel.intro: Payment details and messages are encrypted in this browser and sealed to each reader. A node holds the fact that an entry exists, who wrote it and when — never its content.
tradeChannel.notPublished: You have not published an encryption key, so nobody can seal payment details or messages to you yet. Publishing one asks your wallet to sign the same message twice — the second signature is the check that your wallet signs deterministically, without which a key derived today could not be derived again.
tradeChannel.keyMismatch: Your wallet now derives a different encryption key from the one published on the network. Publishing the new one lets people reach you again and will not recover anything sealed under the old key — those grants are already replicated and cannot be re-addressed.
tradeChannel.counterpartyNotEnrolled: The other party has not published an encryption key yet, so there is nothing to seal a channel to. They publish one the first time they open this trade. Nothing is wrong on your side and nothing here will change until they do.
tradeChannel.grantsUnreadable: This channel has readers, and none of the grants on it are addressed to your current encryption key. The entries below exist and are not empty; they are unreadable here. That happens when the channel was started before you published this key.
tradeChannel.nothingWritten: Nothing has been written into this channel yet.
tradeChannel.sealed: Sealed. This browser holds no key that opens it — that is not the same as it being empty.
tradeChannel.connectPrompt: Connect a wallet — a channel answers only to the settlement's own parties.
tradeChannel.keyPublished: Your encryption key is published. Anyone you trade with can now seal payment details and messages to it, and you can open them on any device this wallet is on.
tradeChannel.channelStarted: Channel key generated and granted to both parties.

placeOrder.ordersRecord: <link>Your orders</link> are what the node reports, and are the record of anything placed here.
placeOrder.missingAd: This advertisement could not be found on the node — it may have been paused, filled, or never existed.
placeOrder.errConnectSign: Connect a wallet that can sign messages before placing an order.
placeOrder.errNoPrice: This advertisement has no price right now, so there is nothing to agree to.
placeOrder.reservationOpenFailed: Your reservation was accepted, but opening the settlement failed: {reason} You can finish it from the trade room.
placeOrder.releasableFalse: This advertisement settles in a mint the escrow program's fee treasuries do not hold. A trade in it can be reserved, funded and approved, and then cannot be released: the release pays the settlement fee into token accounts for a different mint and the runtime rejects it. The tokens are not lost — either party can return them to the merchant's vault — but the trade cannot complete on this deployment.
placeOrder.releasableUnknown: Could not read the escrow program's fee configuration, so whether this mint can be released is unknown — not a claim that it cannot.
placeOrder.connectFirst: Connect a wallet first — a reservation is a signed claim on this merchant's liquidity, and only your wallet can make it.
placeOrder.twoPrompts: Two wallet prompts: the reservation, then the settlement. The reservation lapses 30 minutes after you sign it if the trade has not moved.
placeOrder.methodNote: A ReservationRequest carries no payment method, so the rail you picked is not recorded by this signature — the merchant sends the account to pay into through the trade channel once the settlement is open.

settings.defaultMarketChosen: The currency the exchange opens on, in this browser.
settings.defaultMarketNone: No market chosen yet — the exchange opens on whichever you last browsed.
settings.themeNote: Dark only for now — light mode is on the roadmap

settings.readErrorGeneric: Couldn't read your subscription from your access node.
settings.signerUnavailable: Reconnect your wallet — the signing provider is not available.
settings.neverPublished: This wallet has never published a subscription. That is not the same as having turned everything off — it has made no statement at all.
settings.noDestination: No delivery destination is attached to this subscription, so nothing is actually sent anywhere. Enabling a category records what you want; delivery needs an address sealed to a registered notification gateway, which this app cannot yet create.

settings.starHint: ★ marks the rails your node associates with this country.
settings.fillEvery: Fill every field — a partial account cannot be paid into.
settings.chooseHeld: Choose where the account is held, then which rail it is on.

settings.askingRails: Asking your node which rails exist…

account.nodeUnreachable: Could not reach your access node.
account.signerUnavailable: Reconnect your wallet — the signing provider is not available.
account.mnConnect: Connect a wallet. A merchant name is a claim signed by your key, not an account setting — there is nothing to set until a wallet is connected.
account.mnIntro: The name shown beside your advertisements. It is published as a signed identity claim (OFS-5000), so it belongs to your wallet and follows it to every OpenFiat application — not to this site.
account.currentName: Current name {name}, set {date}. Publishing a new one does not erase it: claims are immutable, so the replacement records which claim it supersedes and the old name stays readable in your history. That is deliberate — a merchant cannot rename away from a bad record.
account.mnFooter: Your wallet signs the claim; nothing is sent on chain and no transaction fee is paid. The claim is not verified by anyone — a display name is self-asserted, and the protocol does no document or business checks at any level.
account.avConnect: Connect a wallet. An avatar is a claim signed by your key, so there is nothing to set until a wallet is connected.
account.imageTooBig: That image is {kb} KB. Keep it under {max} KB.
account.avIntro: The picture shown beside your advertisements. It is stored on IPFS and published as a signed identity claim, so it belongs to your wallet and follows it to every OpenFiat application.
account.avFileHelp: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to {kb} KB.
account.avPlaceholderNote: Until you publish one, your wallet shows the robot on the left. It is drawn from your key on each viewer's own device — nothing is uploaded and no request is made for it — and it is drawn as a placeholder rather than as a picture you chose.
account.avPublicWarning: Anyone can view this image. Content on IPFS is addressed by a hash that travels in public protocol records, and any gateway will serve it to anyone who has that hash — no account and no permission. Do not upload anything you would not publish.
account.avSetOn: Set {date}. Publishing a new one does not erase it: claims are immutable, so the replacement records which claim it supersedes and the old picture stays readable in your history.
account.avFooter: The image is uploaded first, then read back from a gateway to confirm it is really there, and only then does your wallet sign the claim. Nothing goes on chain and no transaction fee is paid.

faucet.metaDescription: Get devnet SOL, mock USDC, mock USDT and OPEN on Solana devnet for testing.
faucet.heroIntro: Sends devnet SOL, mock USDC, mock USDT and OPEN to any Solana devnet address, for testing this app. SOL covers transaction fees and account rent; OPEN is what a protocol role is staked with.
faucet.notReal: These are not real USDC or USDT. They are mock tokens minted solely for testing on Solana devnet, redeemable for nothing, and worth nothing.
faucet.separateService: This faucet is a separate service from the OpenFiat protocol and node network — it only mints test tokens, and never touches escrow, staking, or governance.
faucet.signerUnavailable: Your wallet is not available to sign. Reconnect it and try again.
faucet.faucetUnreachable: Could not reach the faucet service. Try again shortly.
faucet.sentToAddress: {amounts} sent to your address on devnet.
faucet.walletNote: Tokens go to the wallet you have connected. You will be asked to sign a short message proving you control it — no transaction is created, and nothing leaves your wallet.
faucet.connectPrompt: Connect a wallet to request test tokens.
faucet.assetsNote: SOL pays transaction fees and account rent, and OPEN is what a role is staked with — without both, onboarding stops partway. OPEN comes from a finite stash rather than being minted, so it can run out.
faucet.rateLimited: Fixed amount per request, rate-limited per wallet and per IP address — not user-adjustable.

staking.metaDescription: Bond OPEN for your protocol role — merchant, node operator, arbitrator, or service provider.
staking.heroDescription: OPEN secures the coordination layer: every protocol role is bonded. Stake for your role — merchant, node operator, arbitrator, or one of the four service-provider roles. Bonds are enforced by the real openfiat-staking program on Solana devnet.
staking.unstakingFootnote: Unstaking is request_unstake, then withdraw_unstaked once that role's cooldown elapses — the periods are in the table above, one per role. Rewards accrue as pending_rewards and are claimable via claim_rewards — not yet wired to this page's UI, and the schedule that fills that field is an off-chain cranker's, published nowhere this app can read.
staking.stakeMetaDescription: Bond OPEN for a protocol role — merchant, node operator, arbitrator, or service provider.
staking.stakeHeroIntro: Bond OPEN for your protocol role. Bonds are enforced by the staking program on Solana.
staking.noConfig: No staking config exists on this cluster — nothing has set the requirements yet.
staking.noConfigShort: No staking config exists on this cluster.
staking.readErrorGeneric: Couldn't read the staking config from the chain.
staking.connectPromptRoles: Connect a wallet to see what you have staked for each role.
staking.rolesFootnote: Minimums and unbonding periods are read from the deployed StakingConfig account, one of each per role — they are governance-updatable, so neither is a constant in this app. A dash means the account could not be read; it never means zero.
staking.signerError: This wallet connection can't sign — reconnect with a real extension.
staking.noOpenAccount: You don't have an OPEN token account yet — you need OPEN in your wallet before you can stake.
staking.bondedSummary: {amount} OPEN bonded as {role}. Confirmed on devnet.
staking.bondedSummaryNode: {amount} OPEN bonded as {role} for {nodeId}. Confirmed on devnet.
staking.nodeIdNote: Recorded here for display only — the staking program itself has no per-node field.
staking.unbondUnread: The unbonding period could not be read from the chain.
staking.unbondCooldown: Unstaking starts a {label} cooldown for this role.
staking.merchantLockNote: Merchant bonds stay locked while you have active ads, reservations, or unsettled escrow.
staking.readingMin: Reading the minimum from the chain…
staking.realTxNote: Submits a real transaction to the openfiat-staking program on Solana devnet.

merchant.requirement: Required to publish advertisements. OFS-4100 §4 scales the requirement with the position taken; the program enforces the floor.

node.requirement: Stake against a node you operate.

notification-provider.title: Notification Provider stake
notification-provider.requirement: Registration stake for an OFS-1500 notification gateway.

oracle-provider.requirement: Registration stake for an OFS-1500 price oracle.

risk-provider.requirement: Registration stake for an OFS-1500 risk intelligence service.

identity.metaDescription: The identity claims your wallet has actually published, and the reputation counters a node records for it. Both are read live; neither is stored as a score or a level.
identity.heroDescription: What your wallet has published about itself, and what the network has recorded about how it trades. Both are bound to your key rather than to an account, and both travel with it to every OpenFiat application.
identity.levelsFooter: No level is stored against your wallet, and nothing in the protocol is gated on one. A level describes which kinds of claim a wallet has published, so it is something a reader concludes from the list above rather than a status anybody grants.

0.title: Wallet identity
0.body: A valid wallet, authenticated. This is the minimum to use OpenFiat, and §8 is explicit that participation never requires going further than this.

1.title: Verified contact
1.body: One or more communication channels — email, phone, Telegram, Discord, X — published as claims. The specification pairs these with OTP verification; that flow is the wallet application's to run and no node performs it, so a claim marked verified is the publisher saying so.

2.title: Merchant identity
2.body: A display name, business name, brand logo and support contacts, self-published and signed. §8's own caveat is worth repeating: these improve confidence but do not imply regulatory approval, and nobody checks them against a registry.

3.title: Infrastructure provider
3.body: Operational details an infrastructure operator may publish — organisation name, documentation, support and incident contacts — so other operators can identify them. There is no threshold to meet and no bond to post; the specification names no requirement of either kind.

identity.repMetaDescription: Your OpenFiat reputation — wallet-bound, portable, built on 8 objective dimensions.
identity.repPageDescription: No star ratings — reputation is a set of objective, on-chain-verifiable dimensions, bound to your wallet and portable across every OpenFiat application.
identity.repEventsNote: Reputation events (SettlementCompleted, DisputeResolved, PaymentApproved, …) are emitted as signed protocol events and aggregate into the counters above on every OpenFiat application that reads the same wallet.
identity.nodeUnreachable: Could not reach your access node.
identity.claimsConnect: Connect a wallet. A claim is an assertion about a key, so there is no account to open and nothing to show until a key is connected.
identity.noClaims: This wallet has published no claims. That is Level 0, and it is enough to trade — nothing in the protocol requires more.
identity.claimsFooter: Revoked, expired and superseded claims are shown rather than hidden. A claim is never deleted (OFS-5000 §11) — publishing a new value archives the old one — so this is what a counterparty inspecting your wallet sees too.
identity.encryptionKeyNote: Not a wallet key and it holds no funds. Counterparties seal your trade messages and payment details to this, and only your wallet can derive the private half that opens them — on any device, from the same wallet.
identity.repConnect: Connect a wallet. Reputation is bound to a key, not to an account — there is nothing to show until one is connected.
identity.repEmpty: No recorded history for this wallet yet. Reputation is built from completed trades, payment responses and disputes — it starts empty, and an empty record is not a bad one.
identity.repFooter: Counters as the protocol records them (OFS-3000). There are no star ratings and no tiers — reputation is objective, wallet-bound, and portable across every OpenFiat application.

counterparties.metaDescription: How many times you have traded with each wallet, read from a live node by signing a challenge with your own key. Readable only by you.
counterparties.heroDescription: Who you deal with most, and how many times you have traded with each of them. This is your own history and nobody else's: a node will not answer this question for a wallet you cannot prove you hold the key to, so there is no directory of who trades with whom to be looked up, scraped or subpoenaed.
counterparties.title: People you trade with
counterparties.connectPrompt: Connect your wallet. There is no account to sign in to — the key that was party to your trades is the only thing that can read them back, and a node will not answer this question for any other wallet.
counterparties.signPrompt: Reading this asks your wallet to sign a one-time challenge. That signature is how the node knows the history is yours — it proves you hold the key that was party to the trades, and it is the only way to read them.
counterparties.noCompleted: No completed trades on this node yet. A node only counts what it has replicated, so a node that joined the network recently will know about fewer of your trades than happened.
counterparties.startedNeverIntro: Wallets you have opened a settlement with that never reached a release. Not a judgement on anyone — trades are called off for ordinary reasons — but not trading history either, so they are kept out of the list above.
counterparties.tradedTimes: {count, plural, one {You have traded once with this wallet} other {You have traded # times with this wallet}}
counterparties.badgeTitle: Counted from settlements this node has replicated, for your wallet only.
counterparties.badgeDisputedTitle: {count, plural, one {# of your trades with this wallet went to arbitration.} other {# of your trades with this wallet went to arbitration.}}

disputes.metaDescription: OpenFiat dispute arbitration — escrow freezes on filing, staked arbitrators join voluntarily, and votes are cast by commit-and-reveal.
disputes.heroDescription: Filing freezes the escrow immediately and no funds move until the case closes. Cases are decided by independent staked arbitrators who volunteer, review evidence, and vote by commit-and-reveal — not by an assigned judge.
disputes.readError: Could not read disputes from the node
disputes.noDisputes: No disputes yet on the node you are connected to. Filing one happens from a trade room once a settlement is under way.
disputes.yourCasesConnect: Connect your wallet to see which of these cases are yours. A node will not say who is in a case without a signature from someone who is.
disputes.noneInvolve: None of these cases involve the connected wallet.
disputes.casesInvolve: {count, plural, one {One case involves the connected wallet.} other {# cases involve the connected wallet.}}
disputes.showYours: Show which of these are yours
disputes.signsChallenge: — signs a challenge with your wallet.
disputes.detailReadError: Could not read this dispute from the node
disputes.noDispute: This node has no dispute with id “{id}”.
disputes.frozenNote: Escrow for settlement {id} is frozen while this case is open.
disputes.noArbitrator: No arbitrator has joined this case yet.
disputes.arbitratorProgress: {commitments} of {seated, plural, one {# seated arbitrator has} other {# seated arbitrators have}} published a commitment, and {reveals, plural, one {# has} other {# have}} revealed a vote. Who they are is readable by the parties and the panel.
disputes.revealedCount: {reveals} of {seated} seated arbitrators revealed a vote.
disputes.howDecided: There is no assigned judge. Independent arbitrators stake OPEN to join a case they choose and vote by commit-and-reveal, so no one can see how others voted first. Consensus is computed by deterministic rules every implementation reaches identically, and the escrow program executes the result without human approval. Joining a case, committing, and revealing a vote is the arbitrator console's job — see <link>Arbitrate</link>.
disputes.voteCommittedTitle: Commitment published; vote not yet revealed
disputes.accessConnect: The parties and the complaint are readable by the buyer, the seller and the arbitrators seated on this case. Connect the wallet that is in it to see them.
disputes.accessNotParty: The connected wallet is not a party to this case and is not seated on it, so the parties and the complaint stay closed.
disputes.accessSignsChallenge: — signs a challenge with your wallet to unlock the parties and the complaint.

arbitrate.metaDescription: Work a dispute case: join it, then cast the commit-reveal vote that decides the outcome.
arbitrate.heroDescription: Arbitrators choose their own cases and rule with their own OPEN at risk. Joining a case unlocks its evidence; the ruling is a commit-reveal vote, so nobody can follow the crowd. Two votes run side by side — one records the case off-chain, the other decides payout and slashing on chain.
arbitrate.nodeUnreachable: Could not reach the selected node.
arbitrate.reconnectSign: Reconnect your wallet with a real extension to sign.
arbitrate.joinedMsg: Joined the case. Read your cases to see the complaint and the rest of the panel.
arbitrate.committedMsg: Committed "{outcome}". The salt is stored in this browser — you need it to reveal.
arbitrate.noSaltReveal: No salt stored for this case in this browser. Without it the commitment cannot be opened.
arbitrate.connectPrompt: Connect a wallet to work a case. The same key signs your rulings and identifies you to the network.
arbitrate.noDisputesNow: No disputes on this node right now.
arbitrate.yourCasesPrompt: Sign a challenge with your wallet to read the cases you are seated on — the complaint, the rest of the panel, and where each of you has got to. A node will not show any of that to someone who has not joined the case.
arbitrate.notSeatedAny: This wallet is not a party to, or seated on, any case this node knows about.
arbitrate.casesReadable: {count, plural, one {One case readable by this wallet. Select one above to work it.} other {# cases readable by this wallet. Select one above to work it.}}
arbitrate.joinToSeeComplaint: Join this case and read your cases to see the complaint.
arbitrate.onchainResId: On-chain reservation id — the stake-weighted vote that decides payout and slashing
arbitrate.onchainNote: Nothing in the protocol links this to the case id above, so it has to be entered. The on-chain vote uses a different outcome encoding than the off-chain one; this console handles that for you.
arbitrate.enterResId: Enter the on-chain reservation id (a whole number).
arbitrate.commitOffFirst: Commit off-chain first — that is what generates the salt.
arbitrate.noSaltShort: No salt stored for this case in this browser.

ads.metaDescription: Merchant console — publish and manage OpenFiat advertisements backed by your liquidity vaults.
ads.heroDescription: Edit, pause or take down what you have on offer. There is no identity check — the OPEN merchant bond is what is at risk if you do not settle, and Become a merchant reads yours against the chain's own minimum.
ads.connectPrompt: Connect a wallet to see the advertisements published under it. Your wallet key is your merchant identity — there is no separate account to create.
ads.readError: Could not read advertisements from the node
ads.metricTokensSub: liquidity is per asset — see the table
ads.noAds: This wallet has published no advertisements on the node you are connected to.
ads.probMinZero: The minimum must be greater than zero.
ads.probMaxMin: The maximum must be at least the minimum.
ads.probMethods: Keep at least one payment method — a buyer needs a way to pay.

problem.chooseToken: Choose the token you will be paid in.
problem.tokenUnnamed: Your node does not name this token, so its precision is unknown. Choose another.
problem.chooseFiat: Choose the fiat currency you will trade against.
problem.fixedPricePositive: Enter a fixed price greater than 0.
problem.priceMaxDecimals: A price cannot carry more than 12 decimal places.
problem.enterPremium: Enter a premium — 0 tracks the oracle mid exactly.
problem.premiumRange: A premium must be between -{limit}% and +{limit}%.
problem.priceDecimalsRange: Price decimals must be a whole number between 0 and 12.
problem.enterTotal: Enter the total amount you are putting on offer.
problem.maxAtLeastMin: The maximum order must be at least the minimum.
problem.minLargerThanTotal: The minimum order is larger than the total on offer, so no order could be filled.
problem.maxLargerThanTotal: The maximum order is larger than the total on offer.
problem.selectMethod: Select at least one payment method.
problem.atMostMethods: An advertisement can list at most {max}.
problem.backingNoVault: This wallet has no liquidity vault for that token, so nothing backs this advertisement — every reservation against it would fail. Open one from Wallet → Deposit first.
problem.backingShort: Your vault holds {available} available, less than the {total} on offer here.

ads.publishNoWallet: Connect a wallet before publishing — it is what signs the advertisement.
ads.publishNoAsset: The token's precision comes from your node's mint table, and that answer is not in hand. Reload once the node is reachable.
ads.postedNote: Signed by your wallet and accepted by the node, which gossips it to the rest of the network. Edit it, pause it or take it down from My Ads.
ads.fixedExplain: One price, until you change it
ads.floatingExplain: Tracks the oracle mid, refreshed continuously
ads.fixedPriceNote: Signed at exactly the precision you type: {count, plural, one {# decimal place} other {# decimal places}}. A fixed price does not move until you edit it from My Ads.
ads.premiumNote: Applied over the median of every current oracle record for this pair. 0 tracks the mid exactly.
ads.priceDecimalsNote: How many places the resolved price is quoted to — 2 for most currencies, 0 for ones with no subunit in daily use. Asked rather than inferred: a floating ad carries no typed price to take it from, and a currency-to-decimals table here would mis-round every currency missing from it.
ads.totalNote: Checked against your on-chain liquidity vault for this mint, against its <avail>available</avail> balance — the only figure a reservation can draw on. A vault's lifetime total includes tokens that have already settled and left. <vaults>Your vaults</vaults> are on the Wallet page.
ads.threeInAsset: All three are in {asset}, not in {fiat} — that is the unit the record carries them in.
ads.countryNote: Only used to order the suggestions below: your node knows which rails that country actually uses. It is not part of the advertisement — the record carries payment methods and a currency, and no country.
ads.methodsLabel: Payment methods buyers can pay you with (up to {max})
ads.noTimeLimit: There is no payment-time-limit setting here. On Binance a merchant picks one; on this protocol the payment window belongs to the reservation and is set by the node, so an advertisement has no field for it and this screen does not pretend to offer one.
ads.reviewSell: Sell — you sell crypto for fiat
ads.reviewBuy: Buy — you buy crypto with fiat
ads.bondNote: This screen does not read your merchant bond, so it cannot tell you whether the node will accept this. Check where you stand on <link>Become a merchant</link>.
ads.backingChecked: Your vault backing for this token was checked on the previous step.
ads.backingShortStep: Your vault backing for this token is short — see step 3.
ads.postingNote: Posting costs one wallet signature. Everything above is local until then.
ads.connectToPost: Connect a wallet to post — it is what signs the advertisement.
ads.backingUnkeyed: Connect a wallet and pick an asset to check backing
ads.backingError: Could not reach the cluster — backing unverified, not unbacked
ads.backingNone: No vault for this token on this wallet
ads.newMetaDescription: Publish a new OpenFiat advertisement — ad type and asset, price, amount and limits, payment methods, then confirm.
ads.newHeroIntro: Five steps, in the order every P2P desk asks for them: ad type and asset, price, amount and limits, payment methods, then review. Your progress is saved as a draft in this browser and nothing is signed until the last screen. New to this? <link>See what it takes to be a merchant</link>.
ads.ppError: Could not read the current book, so there is nothing to compare this price against. That is a failure to ask, not a finding that the market is empty.
ads.ppOnly: Nobody else is advertising {asset}/{fiat} on the {side} side. Yours would be the only one, which means it takes every order in this corridor — and sets the price.
ads.ppAllFixed: {count, plural, one {# other advertisement} other {# other advertisements}} in this market, all fixed-price. There is no floating premium to compare yours against.
ads.ppFloatingRange: {count, plural, one {# other floating advertisement} other {# other floating advertisements}} here quote between {low} and {high} over the oracle mid. Yours is {mine}. <muted>Where that lands for a buyer depends on the mid, which this screen does not read.</muted>
ads.ppNonePriceable: {count, plural, one {# other advertisement} other {# other advertisements}} in this market, none of them currently priceable — so there is nothing to compare against yet.
ads.ppRanked: #{rank} of {total} at {price} {fiat}. The best {bestLabel} here is {best} {fiat}. Position in the live book as it stands, not a forecast — it moves when anyone reprices.
ads.apAskingTokens: Asking your node which tokens it names…
ads.apRefError: Couldn't ask your access node which tokens exist ({message}). <retry>Try again</retry>
ads.apRefErrorSub: This says nothing about which tokens are tradeable — only that we could not ask.

ads.apFooter: Names and precisions come from your node's mint table, and the address is what the advertisement carries. becomeMerchant.metaDescription: What it takes to advertise on OpenFiat: a wallet, the on-chain OPEN merchant bond, and an account to be paid into. Every requirement read live from the chain.
becomeMerchant.heroDescription: Three things, and the screen reads all three rather than describing them. There is no application and no identity check — the bond is what is at risk if you do not settle.

standing.bondNoConfig: No staking config exists on this cluster, so nothing has set a merchant minimum yet.
standing.bondConnect: Connect a wallet to see what it has bonded.

standing.bondNothing: Nothing bonded for the merchant role on this wallet.

standing.accountIncomplete: Every saved account is missing at least one field, so a buyer could not pay into it.

becomeMerchant.req1Body: It signs every advertisement and every settlement, and it is the merchant identity the network sees. There is no account to create and no identity check.
becomeMerchant.useConnect: Use Connect wallet in the header.
becomeMerchant.req2BodyNoConfig: Bonded OPEN is what a merchant has at risk if they do not settle. The requirement lives on chain, in the staking program's own config.
becomeMerchant.req2Body: {minimum} OPEN, bonded for the merchant role. It stays locked while you hold the role and takes {unbonding} to release after you unbond. Read from StakingConfig on chain — this app keeps no copy of the figure.
becomeMerchant.devnetBondNote: On devnet this step cannot actually be finished: the OPEN mint's authority is permanently unset, so no wallet can obtain any and the token transfer has nothing to move. Creating the stake account works; funding it does not. That is a fact about this cluster, not a limitation of the form.
becomeMerchant.req3Body: At least one account you receive fiat into. When a buyer takes your sell order you nominate one of these, and they see each field separately so they can copy it without retyping.
becomeMerchant.savedHereNote: Saved in this browser and nowhere else. Nothing publishes them, and clearing your site data removes them — so this step is a fact about this device, not about the network.
becomeMerchant.adsReading: Reading your advertisements from the node…
becomeMerchant.adsConnectPrompt: Connect a wallet to see your advertisements.
becomeMerchant.adsNodeError: Could not reach a node to read your advertisements. That says nothing about whether you have any.
becomeMerchant.adsNone: You have no advertisements on this node yet.
becomeMerchant.adsCount: {count, plural, one {You have # advertisement on this node.} other {You have # advertisements on this node.}}
becomeMerchant.notEnforcedNote: Nothing above is enforced by this screen, and the node does not refuse an advertisement from an unbonded wallet. What the bond buys is a counterparty's reason to trust you: it is the stake that is at risk if you take payment and do not release. Posting without it is allowed and visibly unbacked.

walletForms.signerError: This wallet connection can't sign — reconnect with a real extension.
walletForms.failedLookup: This is a failed lookup, not a zero balance.
walletForms.depMetaDescription: Move tokens from your wallet into a liquidity vault on Solana devnet.
walletForms.depHeroIntro: Fund the inventory that backs your sell advertisements. A real transaction on Solana devnet.
walletForms.invalidAddress: That is not a valid Solana address.
walletForms.noDecimals: Could not read this mint's decimals.
walletForms.depBanned: The escrow program rejected this deposit because this wallet is banned. A ban blocks deposits only — withdrawing what you already hold is unaffected.
walletForms.depDoneSummary: {amount} moved from your wallet into your liquidity vault{created, select, true {, and the vault was created in the same transaction} other {}}{wrapped, select, true {, wrapped and unwrapped along the way so nothing was left behind} other {}}. Your Available balance rose by the full amount and can back a sell advertisement now.
walletForms.depIntro1: This moves tokens out of your wallet and into a liquidity vault owned by the escrow program. It is not a transfer between your own accounts.
walletForms.depIntro2: While the tokens sit there, the program can reserve them against a buyer's order and release them on settlement without asking you to sign again — that is what makes a sell advertisement fillable. Anything not reserved stays yours to withdraw at any time, and no one else can withdraw it.
walletForms.depNamesNote: Names come from the node you are connected to, not from this app — no devnet mint here publishes on-chain metadata of its own. Check the address. SOL's address is wrapped SOL's, which is what the vault actually holds.
walletForms.depCannotObtain: You cannot obtain this token on devnet, so a deposit will only work if you already hold some.
walletForms.depLookupErrorTitle: Could not read this mint from devnet
walletForms.depNoTokenAccount: This wallet has no token account for this mint, so it holds none of it and there is nothing to deposit.
walletForms.depWrapNote: Your wallet holds {sol} SOL. {reserved} of it is held back for the transaction fee{createVault, select, true { and the rent for the two accounts your vault is made of} other {}}{hasRefund, select, true {, of which {refunded} is rent for the wrapped-SOL account and comes straight back when it is closed in the same transaction} other {}}.{hasWrapped, select, true { You also already hold {wrapped} wrapped SOL, which this deposit spends before wrapping anything new.} other {}}
walletForms.depTooManyDecimals: Enter a number with no more than {decimals} decimal places — this mint cannot represent a smaller amount.
walletForms.depVaultCurrent: Your vault for this mint currently has <n>{available}</n> available.{after, select, true { After this deposit it will have <n>{newAvailable}</n>.} other {}}
walletForms.depNoVaultYet: You have no vault for this mint yet. One will be created in the same transaction, which costs a small amount of SOL in rent, and the deposit will land in it.
walletForms.depWrapMechanics: The escrow program can only hold a token account, so this transaction wraps your SOL, makes the deposit, and closes the wrapped account again — in that order, in one transaction. You never hold wrapped SOL, and a failure at any step leaves nothing behind, because either the whole transaction lands or none of it does.
walletForms.depFooterNote: One transaction to the openfiat-escrow program on Solana devnet. Your wallet will show you exactly what it signs.
walletForms.wdMetaDescription: Take tokens back out of a liquidity vault on Solana devnet.
walletForms.wdHeroIntro: Move available vault balance back to your own wallet. A real transaction on Solana devnet.
walletForms.wdInsufficient: The program rejected this withdrawal: the vault's available balance is lower than the amount requested. Reserved and pending-settlement balances cannot be withdrawn until those trades close.
walletForms.wdDoneSummary: {amount} left the vault and is {asSol, select, true {in your wallet as SOL — the wrapped-SOL account it passed through was closed in the same transaction} other {in your wallet's token account}}. The vault's Available balance fell by the same amount, so anything you advertise against it should come down too.
walletForms.wdConnect: Connect a wallet to withdraw from the liquidity vaults it owns.
walletForms.wdReadError: Could not read your vaults from Solana devnet
walletForms.wdReadErrorSub: The lookup failed, so this is not a statement that you have nothing to withdraw.
walletForms.wdNoVaults: This wallet owns no liquidity vaults, so there is nothing to withdraw.
walletForms.wdNoVaultsSub: That is the chain's answer, not a failed lookup.
walletForms.wdIntro1: This takes tokens back out of the escrow program's custody and returns them to your wallet, in one transaction you sign — into your own token account, or as plain SOL if the vault holds SOL.
walletForms.wdIntro2: You can only withdraw what is <avail>Available</avail>. Balance reserved against an open order, or already funded into a trade escrow, stays where it is until that trade settles, is cancelled, or expires — the program rejects a withdrawal that reaches into it.
walletForms.wdNothingAvailableCommitted: This vault has nothing available. Its balance is committed to open trades.
walletForms.wdNothingAvailableSettled: This vault has nothing available. Everything it held has already settled away.
walletForms.wdTooManyDecimals: Enter a number with no more than {decimals} decimal places — this mint cannot represent a smaller amount.
walletForms.wdOverAvailable: More than this vault has available ({available}).
walletForms.wdReservedNote: A further {reserved} is reserved and cannot be withdrawn.
walletForms.wdUnwrapNote: Arrives as <sol>SOL</sol>, spendable straight away. The program can only pay into a wrapped-SOL token account, so this transaction opens one, takes the withdrawal into it, and closes it again — all before you see the result. You never hold wrapped SOL, and nothing is left behind if any step fails, because all of it is one transaction.
walletForms.wdExistingWrapped: You are already holding {existing} wrapped SOL. Closing the account returns that to you as SOL as well, so expect {total} SOL in total.
walletForms.wdTokenAccountNote: Goes to your own associated token account for this mint, created in the same transaction if you do not have one. To send it anywhere else, transfer from your wallet afterwards — the program only pays out to a token account of this exact mint.
walletForms.wdFooterNote: One transaction to the openfiat-escrow program on Solana devnet.

reviews.notSettled: A trade can be reviewed once the merchant has approved the payment. Cancelled, rejected and disputed trades cannot be — a review is one party's opinion of a trade that happened, and a disputed outcome is not this protocol's to summarise as stars.
reviews.connectPrompt: Connect the wallet that was party to this trade to review it.
reviews.notParty: The node answered, and this wallet is not a party to this trade — so there is nothing here for it to review. Only the buyer and the seller may, one review each.
reviews.signerError: This wallet connection cannot sign — reconnect it and try again.
reviews.published: Published. It is gossiped to the rest of the network from here.
reviews.checkPrompt: Whether you have already reviewed this trade is readable only by you — the public feed carries no author and no trade id, on purpose. Sign once to check.
reviews.publishedAbout: Published about {who}. Others see the stars, the words and the day — not your wallet and not this trade.
reviews.commentNote: {count}/{max}. Published to everyone and stored by every node forever — it cannot be deleted, only replaced. Put nothing in it you would not publish under your wallet: the node hides who wrote a review, and cannot hide a name you type into one yourself.
reviews.footerNote: A review changes no reputation score. Reputation is recomputed by every node from signed settlements and disputes and cannot be talked up or down; this is an opinion, and the two are shown apart because they are not the same kind of claim.

merchants.metaDescription: Everyone advertising a trade on OpenFiat, read from the advertisement book (OFS-2100) your access node holds — the pairs they quote, the payment rails they take, and the trading record the protocol computes for them.
merchants.heroDescription: Every wallet currently advertising a trade, as your access node's advertisement book reports it. There is no merchant register in this protocol and no application to be listed — publishing an advertisement is what puts a wallet here, and withdrawing every advertisement is what removes it.
merchants.readError: Could not read the advertisement book from {label}.
merchants.nothingToShow: Nothing to show — the book could not be read.
merchants.emptyBook: No wallet has published an advertisement to this node yet.
merchants.footerNote: A merchant is a wallet that has published an advertisement. There is no merchant register in the protocol, so this list is everyone currently offering a trade — including those who have paused — and a wallet that deletes its last advertisement leaves it. Names and pictures appear only where the wallet published them as identity claims; the rest are drawn from the key itself.

offeringTitle.advertising: At least one advertisement is Active.
offeringTitle.onVacation: Every advertisement is in Vacation — a pause the merchant set themselves (OFS-2100 §16).
offeringTitle.disabled: Every advertisement is Disabled: manually turned off, or automatically because liquidity hit zero (OFS-2100 §18).

merchants.recNodeError: Your access node did not answer for this wallet.
merchants.recEmpty: This node has no settlements, disputes or payments involving this wallet. It has advertised but not yet traded — or has traded only through peers this node has not replicated from.
merchants.recCompletionHint: Completed settlements ÷ started settlements (OFS-3000 §8). Not a rating.
merchants.recAnsweredHint: How often this wallet, as merchant, approved or rejected a buyer's payment declaration at all (OFS-3000 §13).
merchants.recMeanAnswerHint: Measured between two signed events: the buyer declaring payment and the merchant ruling on it. Not an advertised turnaround.
merchants.recMissedHint: Reservations this wallet requested and let expire.
merchants.recFooter: Computed by your access node from settlements, disputes and reservations it has replicated — nothing here is asserted by the merchant. A node that has seen less of the network will report less.
merchants.profileReadError: Could not read this wallet's advertisements from {label}.
merchants.nameSelfPublished: A name this wallet published about itself (MerchantName claim). Nothing verifies it.
merchants.profileNoAds: This wallet has no advertisements on this node. It may have deleted them, or this node may not have replicated them.
merchants.noReviews: No reviews of this wallet on this node. Only a party to a settled trade may publish one, once per trade — and reviews are gossiped, so a node that has replicated less of the network reports fewer of them.
merchants.reviewsFooter: Signed by somebody who really settled a trade with this wallet, and nothing more than that. The author and the trade are deliberately not published — both parties may review the same trade, so either would rebuild the counterparty graph the protocol withholds. The date is the day, not the moment, for the same reason. This is opinion; the trading record beside it is computed from signed events and cannot be talked up or down.
merchants.profileMetaDescription: A wallet advertising on OpenFiat: the advertisements it has published, what counterparties said about it, and the trading record your access node computes for it.

pair.metaDesc: Convert {label} to {currency} peer-to-peer at {rate} {currency} per {label}.{advertiserPhrase} Escrow enforced by Solana programs — OpenFiat never takes custody of your {currency}.

pair.advertisersLine: {advertisers, plural, one {# advertiser is} other {# advertisers are}} trading {label} against {currency} right now. There is no exchange in the middle: you pick someone whose price and limits suit you, and the {currency} moves between your own accounts{methods, select, none {} other { using {methods}}}{more, select, yes { and others} other {}}.
pair.noAdvertisersLine: Nobody is advertising {label} against {currency} on this node right now. A node counts only the advertisements it has replicated, so a node that joined recently knows about fewer than exist — and an empty corridor is an opening rather than a closure: the first merchant in one sets the price.
pair.escrowLine: Your {label} is locked in a Solana escrow program before any {currency} is sent. It releases when the receiving side confirms the money arrived, and if they do not, independent arbitrators who have staked OPEN decide it. Nobody at OpenFiat can release escrow early, freeze it, or take custody of your {currency} at any point.

pair.noOtherCurrencies: {label} is not priced in any other currency right now.
pair.rateMedianAll: Median across every unexpired oracle record

pair.rateContext: {median} (OFS-7000 §11), good until {until}. Advertisers price above or below it, so the rate you get is the one on the offer you accept — compare below.
pair.unreachableRate: The access node could not be reached, so there is no rate to show. This says nothing about whether {label}/{currency} is priced — only that we could not ask.

pair.noOracleRate: No oracle publishes {label}/{currency} on this node, so there is no median rate for it. That is not a temporary outage: it is a corridor nobody prices yet. Merchants can still advertise the pair at a fixed price of their own choosing.
